# Fixtures that must never be auto-run by a pull request's scoped conformance.
#
# ci.yml scopes a PR's conformance to the fixtures the PR touched. Some fixtures
# cannot pass in CI no matter what the PR changed - the blocker is the test
# environment or the job's time budget, not the diff - so running them turns
# every PR that touches them red and bills Azure for the privilege. They are
# listed here and subtracted from the PR scope, with the reason on each.
#
# Same format as conformance-matrix.txt: one fixture per line, '#' comments and
# blank lines ignored. A name may NOT appear in both files - conformance-scope.sh
# fails the run if one does, so the two cannot drift into disagreement.
#
# This file does NOT affect push-to-main or nightly. Those are driven purely by
# conformance-matrix.txt; a fixture absent from that file already does not run.
#
# Removing a line here is how a fixture becomes PR-eligible again - do it once
# the blocker below is gone.

# --- Blocked by the CI environment: no diff can make these pass -------------

# Needs a real owned domain (Azure serves an ownership challenge the CI
# subscription cannot answer).
custom-hostname-binding

# Azure validates an App Service certificate against a verified custom domain on
# the referenced plan; with no verified domain, no certificate is accepted.
app-service-certificate

# The conformance subscription has a dedicated-VM quota of 0, and an App Service
# plan of ANY sku runs on dedicated VMs - verified 2026-08-28 against both B1
# (Basic) and F1 (Free); both are refused identically:
#
#   Code: Unauthorized
#   Operation cannot be completed without additional quota.
#   Current Limit (Total VMs): 0 / Amount required for this deployment: 1
#
# So no plan can be created there, and every Microsoft.Web fixture that needs one
# fails on the plan rather than on anything the plugin did. Raising the
# subscription's "Total Regional vCPUs"/App Service quota is the only unblock;
# remove these four lines when that lands. AZURE::Web::StaticSite is unaffected
# (Static Web Apps are serverless) and stays in PR scope.
#
# CRUD for all four is covered by the mocked integration tests; run live against
# a quota-bearing subscription with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=app-service-plan
app-service-plan
web-app
function-app
web-app-slot

# virtual-hub passes locally end to end (68m50s) but cannot pass in CI. ARM
# refuses DeleteVirtualHub while routingState is still Provisioning, which runs
# ~11 min past the create LRO reporting Succeeded, so the CRUD phase measures
# ~59 min - longer than the OIDC client assertion stays valid. The run dies in the
# final phase with:
#
#   AADSTS700024: Client assertion is not within its valid time range
#
# The plugin waits for the router correctly (see VirtualHub.Delete); this is a
# credential-lifetime limit, not a plugin bug. Remove this line once CI can
# refresh auth mid-phase. Run locally with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=virtual-hub TIMEOUT=90
virtual-hub

# --- Exceed the conformance-tests job's timeout-minutes: 120 ----------------
# Measured lifecycles: vpn-gateway ~60 min, the two virtual-network-gateway
# fixtures ~60-90 min, and a lifecycle runs create + update + destroy +
# recreate + OOB-delete. scripts/ci/run-conformance-phase.sh already carries
# their per-command budgets, so raising the job cap is the only change needed to
# make them runnable.
vpn-gateway
virtual-network-gateway
virtual-network-gateway-connection

# --- Wave 2 -----------------------------------------------------------------

# Management group operations are tenant-scoped, and no principal on the test
# subscription has any role assignment above subscription scope - verified with
#   az role assignment list --scope /subscriptions/<sub> --include-inherited
# which returns only subscription-scoped Owner/Contributor/Reader rows, and with
#   az account management-group list
#   -> AuthorizationFailed: ... does not have authorization to perform action
#      'Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/read' over scope
#      '/providers/Microsoft.Management'
# The handlers are implemented and unit-tested; they cannot be exercised live
# until a principal is granted a role at the tenant root. Remove these two lines
# when that lands. Run locally against a tenant-root-capable login with:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=management-group
management-group
management-group-subscription-association

# A Managed HSM bills at roughly $3.20/hour from the moment it is created - by
# far the most expensive resource in the suite - and takes 20-30 min to
# provision. It also has soft-delete permanently on with a 7-day minimum
# retention, so the conformance lifecycle's OOB-delete-then-recreate would hit
# "name already in a soft-deleted state" unless the purge succeeds first. A run
# that is killed mid-lifecycle therefore leaks a resource costing ~$2,300/month
# until someone notices. Not worth running on every PR that touches the fixture.
# The handler is implemented and unit-tested. Run it deliberately, and check
# afterwards that nothing is left in `az keyvault list-deleted --resource-type mhsm`:
#   make conformance-test-crud TEST=managed-hsm TIMEOUT=120
managed-hsm
